steps.title: Open the Structure page
steps.narration: Let's open the Structure page — this is where Tapeology fetches real stock price history straight from Yahoo Finance, no sign-up or fee required, and turns it into support-and-resistance levels.
steps.point_out: A 'Fetch from Yahoo Finance' panel sits at the top of the page, with a simpler, read-only 'Load' form just below it.

expect.text: Choose a symbol and an as-of time, then Load, to see its S/R levels and confluence zones.

steps.title: Type in a stock symbol
steps.narration: Type in a stock symbol to fetch its real history — we'll use AAPL.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field in the fetch panel now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Choose a real timeframe
steps.narration: Pick a timeframe. Six real choices are on offer here — weekly down to 1-minute, including an honestly self-computed 4-hour view — and every one of them is genuine, never invented.

steps.title: Set the start of the date range
steps.narration: Set the start of the date range to fetch, in UTC.
steps.point_out: The Start field is filled in.

steps.title: Set the end of the date range
steps.narration: And the end of that range.
steps.point_out: The End field is filled in, and the fetch button is no longer greyed out.

steps.title: Fetch real bars from Yahoo Finance
steps.narration: Click once, and the app pulls real historical prices straight from Yahoo Finance — no sign-up, no API key, no fee — and draws the chart immediately.
steps.point_out: A real candlestick chart appears with dashed support-and-resistance lines, and a 'Confluence zones' list below shows Class A/B/C zones with scores drawn from several real timeframes together.

expect.text: Level lines span every recorded timeframe.

steps.title: See exactly where the data came from
steps.narration: A small badge above the chart names exactly where this data came from, so it's never a mystery.
steps.point_out: A dark chip reading 'feed' next to 'Yahoo Finance' in bold sits cleanly above the chart.

steps.title: Ask for the same window again
steps.narration: Ask for that exact same window again, and it comes right back instantly — this history is already safely stored, so there's nothing new to fetch and nothing gets duplicated.
steps.point_out: The identical chart and confluence zones reappear immediately.

expect.text: Level lines span every recorded timeframe.

steps.title: Look up the same stock a simpler way
steps.narration: The page also has a simpler, read-only Load form below the fetch panel — let's look up AAPL through that instead.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field in the Load form now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Set the as-of time
steps.narration: Enter a point in time to check its levels as of.
steps.point_out: The As-of field is filled in.

steps.title: Load the same real levels from storage
steps.narration: Click Load, and the same real support-and-resistance levels and confluence zones appear again, this time read straight from storage rather than a fresh fetch.
steps.point_out: The candlestick chart and confluence-zone list reappear for AAPL.

steps.title: Confirm the rest of the app still works
steps.narration: Finally, a quick check that nothing else broke while this chapter was being finished: the replay studies lab — where past trade setups get tested against history — still opens exactly as it always has.
steps.point_out: The 'Replay studies' heading renders cleanly at the top of the page.
